q: What is the CBAM default value for Indian steel billets and ingots?
title: CBAM default value: Indian billets, ingots
short: Indian non-alloy semi-finished steel under CN 7207 carries 4.270 or 4.320 t CO2e per tonne depending on the subheading, and ingots under CN 7206 carry 2.640. Direct emissions only. Add the 10% mark-up for goods imported in 2026.
audience: Indian billet, bloom, slab and ingot producers and their EU buyers

sections.h: India default values, t CO2e per tonne
ul: CN 7206 10 00 ingots of iron and non-alloy steel: 2.640
CN 7224 alloy steel ingots and semi-finished: 7.320 to 7.350
CN 7218 stainless ingots and semi-finished: 6.490 to 6.530

p: The listed values are increased by a mark-up: 10% for 2026, 20% for 2027 and 30% from 2028. Goods imported in 2026 always take the 2026 mark-up.
Within CN 7207 the value changes by subheading, which depends on carbon content and cross-section. Get the exact eight-digit code from your EU importer's customs declaration before quoting a figure.

senseible: Senseible reads coal, coke, gas, electricity and freight invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record per site, so an actual figure you send an EU buyer can be traced back to the documents behind it. It does not file CBAM declarations.
